newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Trust Fund to be set up by Q1 1997.
newsitem.headline: Thai Trust Fund to be set up by Q1 1997.

text.p: The Thai Trust Fund, a vehicle designed to help foreign investors circumvent Thai corporate ownership limits, will be launched no later than the first quarter of 1997, the head of the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said on Thursday.
Pakorn Malakul Na Ayudhya, secretary-general of the SEC, told reporters the regulation was published in the Royal Gazette on October 4 with effect on October 5.

Pakorn said the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) is now required to submit a proposal on the launching of the Thai Trust Funds to the SEC within 30 days in its capacity as the major shareholder of the scheme.
The licence will then be given to the SET so that it could set up, Pakorn said.

Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda has said he expects foreign investors to be keen to buy units in the Thai incorporated mutual funds, through which they could buy shares above current 25-49 percent foreign ownership limits set for listed Thai companies.
